# Tiny real V8 remap controls: distinct terminal-map-route repair

Research preparation only; no repair proof, provider run, new compiler invocation, CPU check or product edit has occurred. Original independently approved twelve files and failed `/tmp/starship-native-provider-control.FWIPCK` remain immutable. Its actual public Vite build resolved and emitted a 685-byte control.mjs and 967-byte external map, but the following assertion wrongly demanded a final LF. It failed before any Vitest run. The exact terminal comment is present with no trailing newline. This failure does not establish provider remap behavior. All actual private bytes/outputs/owner/source/tool before-and-after receipts are durably preserved under `native-provider-remap-controls-failed-map-route-artifacts` with a lossless origin/digest manifest. The two entire original flight files, root V8 provider/floors/config and budgets stay unchanged. This private fixture cannot qualify production coverage or a native flight project by itself.

The repair adds `external-map-route.mjs`, its separate `route-control-proof.mjs` and `compile-origin.json`; the new candidate has fifteen files at a distinct research path. `run-owned.mjs` requires `RUN_NATIVE_PROVIDER_CONTROLS=1` and the externally supplied exact independent candidate manifest path plus SHA256 through `NATIVE_PROVIDER_TEMPLATE_MANIFEST` and `NATIVE_PROVIDER_TEMPLATE_MANIFEST_SHA256`. It verifies the entire inventory and bytes against that parent pin before creating a unique mode-0700 `/tmp/starship-native-provider-control.*`, materializes without overwriting, and reuses reviewed `scripts/bench/owned-command.mjs`. Work remains 30 seconds including preparation/tool boundaries; the child receives remaining time, at most 28 seconds, reserving two seconds for postchecks. Cleanup uses existing TERM/KILL/pipe stages (5+2+1 seconds). Inner children use SIGKILL at their shared deadline. Root supervises the whole owner/preparation call and independently verifies all owned PID/start identities nonexecuting before CPU release. No new owner abstraction or automatic retry.

Reuse the exact bytes of the resolved original public Vite ES2022/unminified ESM/external-map compilation; there is no second build. The new owner links the original FAILED child/outcome, original input/Node hashes, full original installed-tools digest, fixture sources and current complete installed-tools equality through `compile-origin.json`. Copy only the actual code/map into the new private artifact directory at the identical relative source layout. Every fixture source must match; each sourceContents resolves at the new layout and must match actual input bytes before provider execution. `compiled-lineage.json` explicitly records original failed episode/reused compilation and actual runtime/map/source hashes, never a forged green build receipt. Source map paths are not edited or normalized. The new cohort removes only the compiler call and replaces the over-specific LF check with the exported exact-route validator; all provider recipes/floors/schema/offset/source controls remain intact.

The exported validator accepts the exact terminal `//# sourceMappingURL=control.mjs.map` with no ending, LF or CRLF, and only one route in the entire actual code. It rejects extra trailing blank lines/code, wrong filename, inline data URL and duplicate routes. It does not modify code or maps. Historical .mjs/.ts/.sh bytes are retained as .txt to keep completed snapshots out of executable tooling; the lossless origin manifest records original name, durable name and digest. `compile-origin.json` supplies that explicit path mapping. The pure proof resolves original map paths to their original virtual source identity and reads the exact retained bytes; the future private setup restores original filenames and relative layout without altering map or source bytes. Before any provider invocation, ONE separately supervised pure `route-control-proof.mjs` must pass all three positive endings and five negatives, then validate the actual retained compiler code/map/sourceContents plus source/origin/outcome digests. This proof uses no compiler/provider/tool inventory and reports the helper/origin hashes. Root owns its bounded command and review; a source draft alone does not count as passed. Its actual reviewed output is a prerequisite for the separate provider-cohort grant.

The protected source has an enum, positive/negative choose, nested positive/small/large/nonpositive branches and neverCalled. A wholly unimported protected source proves full denominator. An actually called outside-core source is included in code/map so excludeAfterRemap must exclude it without report filtering. Unknown/outside-private mapped sources fail closed. Tiny unminified fixture success cannot qualify a differently compiled future graph; that graph needs its own compiler/map/source review.

Four private configs use the installed real Vitest 4.1.11 V8 provider, forks/isolate, one worker, 10-second test/hook limits and zero retry. Native projects explicitly use `experimental.viteModuleRunner:false`; the SSR project explicitly uses true. Their includes are exact tests. No broad research/cache/node_modules match, global alias hook, custom provider, patched provider, fake coverage, production enum rewrite or duplicate-flight cache is used.

`finalize.mjs` reads immutable raw reports. Positive keys must be exactly the two canonical protected source paths, with no compiled artifact or mapped noncore key.
